doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Egypt and classical repertoire abroad
summary: Egyptian audiences respected Sun Ra in 1971; in Germany, Vienna and Russia the band played classics, with a solo for Allen.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When the band went to Egypt in 1971 I think, and — how did those audiences react to the band and the fact that you had a look, Egyptian-looking costuming, and here you are in Egypt. Can you recall what that was like?
Yeah they liked that. They liked the music, they liked — they respect Sun Ra and they called him Sun Ra, and Sun Ra was talking by name to Egyptians and all those things. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
And the music is the same way, they would come to listen to the music because Sun Ra had that spirit that they’d know he wasn’t a phony. You see?

Did you ever have the opposite experience, like there’s a famous incident where the premiere of “The Rite of Spring” by Stravinsky and there was almost a riot in the auditorium in the theater. I wonder if you ever played a gig where people were expecting something else?

Yeah, in the Black Forest it was the same way. We played in Germany in the Black Forest and played classical, Sun Ra would play the classics, and then we was in Vienna so he played their [hums]. But he put it [scats]. So he gave me that solo. So I had to play that while they played the background. And he’d take classical and use it and play. Yeah. Russia and all, we’d play. He could play the classics, so he was a well-rounded musician.
